Compute Projected Precision and Statistical Power for PPI++

Source: R/ppi_power.R
ppi_power.Rd

Evaluates projected PPI++ standard error, effective sample size, variance reduction factor, and (when effect is supplied) two-sided statistical power across grids of human validation sizes n_labeled and/or LLM-human correlations r, directly benchmarked against human-only estimation.

Usage

ppi_power(
  n_labeled,
  n_unlabeled = NULL,
  n_total = NULL,
  effect = NULL,
  sd = NULL,
  r = NULL,
  pilot = NULL,
  term = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05
)

Arguments

n_labeled

Positive integer vector of candidate human validation sample sizes.

n_unlabeled

Optional non-negative numeric vector (or Inf) of unlabeled LLM sample sizes. Ignored if n_total is supplied. Defaults to Inf when n_total is NULL.

n_total

Optional finite total corpus size (n_labeled + n_unlabeled).

effect

Optional non-zero target effect size for power computation.

sd

Positive single-observation SD scaling constant. Inferred from pilot if NULL.

r

Numeric vector of LLM-human score correlations in [0, 1]. Inferred from pilot if NULL.

pilot

Optional pilot "llm_ppi" or continuous "llm_calibration" object from which sd and r are estimated automatically.

term

Optional parameter term name for multi-term "llm_ppi" pilots.

alpha

Two-sided significance level in (0, 1). Default 0.05.

Value

An S3 object of class "llm_ppi_power" containing $grid tibble, $params, $effect, $alpha, and autoplot() support.

Examples

pw <- ppi_power(
  n_labeled = seq(40, 240, by = 40),
  n_total = 1500,
  effect = 0.25,
  sd = 1.2,
  r = c(0.6, 0.8, 0.9)
)
pw
